title: "def self.build" rewritten as "class << self; def build"
expected: Both are the singleton method build; the text and tree change, so movedWithEdit or edited, never reformatted or plain moved.
old:
class Widget
  def self.build(opts)
    new(opts).tap(&:validate!)
  end

  def render
    "<widget>"
  end
end
new:
class Widget
  class << self
    def build(opts)
      new(opts).tap(&:validate!)
    end
  end

  def render
    "<widget>"
  end
end

title: "{ |i| ... }" rewritten as "do |i| ... end" on the same call
expected: The block attaches to each in both versions: reformatted.

    puts i
  end
end

title: "puts items.map { }" rewritten as "puts items.map do ... end"

new:

  puts items.map do |i|
    i * 2
  end
end

title: Extract whose helper returns its last expression
expected: with_tax extracted from total; its value is the implicit return, the caller uses it as its own last expression.
old:
class Invoice
  def total
    subtotal = items.sum(&:price)
    tax = subtotal * rate
    subtotal + tax
  end
end
new:
class Invoice
  def total
    subtotal = items.sum(&:price)
    with_tax(subtotal)
  end

  def with_tax(subtotal)
    tax = subtotal * rate
    subtotal + tax
  end
end

title: Extract called as a bare identifier ("lines = header")
expected: header extracted from render; the call has no receiver and no arguments, so it parses as an identifier.
old:
class Report
  def render
    lines = []
    lines << "Header"
    lines << "=" * 20
    lines.concat(rows)
    lines.join("\n")
  end
end
new:
class Report
  def render
    lines = header
    lines.concat(rows)
    lines.join("\n")
  end

  def header
    lines = []
    lines << "Header"
    lines << "=" * 20
    lines
  end
end

title: Inline of a helper called as a bare identifier
expected: discount inlined into price; it was called bare and returned its last expression.
old:
class Item
  def price
    base - discount
  end

  def discount
    pct = member? ? 0.1 : 0.0
    base * pct
  end
end
new:
class Item
  def price
    pct = member? ? 0.1 : 0.0
    base - base * pct
  end
end

title: LIMIT renamed to MAX, and "<" became "<=" on a line that uses it
expected: renamed LIMIT -> MAX on lines 2 and 9; line 5 also changed its operator, so renamed must not cover line 5.
old:
module Limits
  LIMIT = 10

  def self.ok?(n)
    n < LIMIT
  end

  def self.cap(n)
    [n, LIMIT].min
  end
end
new:
module Limits
  MAX = 10

  def self.ok?(n)
    n <= MAX
  end

  def self.cap(n)
    [n, MAX].min
  end
end
